diagnosis_explanation:
Your colon had cancer. You had surgery to remove part of it.

You also have a low red blood cell count. This is called anemia. You had trouble breathing. This was a lung infection. It happened while you were in the hospital. You have high blood pressure. You also have heart failure. This means your heart does not pump blood well. You have seizures. This means your brain sometimes has bursts of electricity.
medication_rationale:
Coreg 12.5 mg twice daily:
This medicine helps your heart pump blood better. It also lowers your blood pressure. You may feel less tired. You might notice a slower heart rate. This is often normal. Call your doctor if you feel very dizzy or faint. Also call if your breathing gets very difficult.

Lipitor 10 mg every night at bedtime:
This medicine is to help lower your cholesterol. High cholesterol can lead to heart problems. You will not usually feel this medicine working. Your doctor will check your blood with tests. Call your doctor if you get unexplained muscle aches. Also call if your urine becomes dark.

Nitro-Dur patch 0.3 mg per hour one patch daily:
This medicine helps blood flow to your heart muscle. It can help with chest pain. You will wear this patch on your skin. You might get a headache. You could also feel dizzy. Call your doctor if you get severe chest pain. Also call if you have skin irritation under the patch.

Phenergan syrup 6.25 mg every 4 hours as needed:
This medicine can help with nausea or vomiting. It can also make you feel sleepy. You may feel drowsy. This is normal. Call your doctor if you feel very confused. Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Synthroid 0.175 mg daily:
This medicine replaces a hormone your thyroid gland makes. It helps control your body's energy use. You should start to feel more energy. Your mood may also improve. Call your doctor if you get chest pain. Also call if you feel unusually tired.

Zyrtec 10 mg daily:
This medicine is an allergy medicine. It can help with itching or hives. You may feel sleepy from this medicine. This is common. Call your doctor if you feel very restless. Also call if you have a fast heartbeat.

Lamictal 100 mg in the morning:
This medicine is for your seizure disorder. It helps prevent seizures. You may feel dizzy or tired. This is common. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Lamictal 150 mg every night at bedtime:
This medicine is for your seizure disorder. It helps prevent seizures. You may feel dizzy or tired. This is common. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Ferrous sulfate drops 325 mg twice daily:
This medicine is a type of iron. It helps your body make new red blood cells. This can help with anemia, which means you have low red blood cells. You may get constipation or an upset stomach. Call your doctor if your stools look black and sticky.

Nexium 40 mg at breakfast:
This medicine reduces the acid in your stomach. It can help heal stomach or throat problems. You might have an upset stomach. This is common. Call your doctor if you get severe stomach pain. Also call if you have black or bloody stools.

Neurontin 400 mg three times daily:
This medicine can help with nerve pain. It can also help prevent seizures. You may feel dizzy or sleepy. This is common. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing. Also call if you have swelling in your arms or legs.

Lasix 40 mg twice daily:
This medicine helps your body get rid of extra fluid. It is for your heart failure. You will urinate more often. This is normal. Call your doctor if you feel very dizzy. Also call if you get muscle cramps.

Fentanyl patch 50 mcg every 72 hours:
This medicine is a strong pain reliever. It helps manage your pain. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is common. Call your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing. Also call if your skin where the patch is gets very red.

Calcium and vitamin D combination calcium carbonate 500 mg/vitamin D 200 units three times daily:
This medicine gives your body calcium and vitamin D. These are important for your bones. You might get an upset stomach. This is common. Call your doctor if you get severe constipation. Also call if you have frequent headaches.

Bactrim DS 800mg/160 mg tablet every 12 hours (for 3 days):
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights infections. You might get an upset stomach or a rash. This is common. Call your doctor right away if you get a severe rash. Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Levaquin 750 mg once daily (for 3 days):
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights infections. You might get an upset stomach or feel dizzy. This is common. Call your doctor right away if you have tendon pain or swelling. Also call if you have watery diarrhea.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and sore. This is normal.
- Rest is important. Avoid all strenuous activity.
- You can have clear liquids by mouth.
- Your J-tube will give you special food all night.
- Do not drink alcohol.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101 F.
- Your goal is to rest and let your body heal.

**Week 2:**
- Your pain should start to feel a little better.
- You can try walking short distances inside your home.
- Avoid any strenuous activity.
- Continue your clear liquids by mouth.
- Your J-tube will continue to feed you at night.
- Call your doctor if you have bad stomach pain.
- Your goal is to increase walking time a little each day.

**Week 3:**
- You may start to feel more energy this week.
- You can do light activities around the house.
- Do not lift heavy things or do strenuous activity.
- You can try eating soft foods by mouth.
- Your J-tube will still give you food at night.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.
- Your goal is to walk for 10 minutes twice a day.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel stronger this week.
- You can return to most light daily activities.
- Avoid any strenuous activity for now.
- Continue eating soft foods and drinking fluids.
- Your J-tube will continue feeding you at night.
- Call your doctor if you have swelling in your legs.
- Your goal is to walk outside for 15 minutes daily.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel better each week.
- Healing takes time after surgery.
- Follow your doctor's instructions for J-tube feeding.
- Listen to your body and rest when needed.
- Keep up with your follow-up appointments.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Seizure lasting more than 5 minutes: This is a medical emergency.
- Uncontrolled bleeding: Blood loss can be dangerous.
- Not breathing or cannot breathe: Get help right away.
- Severe chest pain or pressure: Call 911 now.
- Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness, trouble speaking.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 101 degrees F: You may have an infection.
- Wound appears infected: Red streaks or pus mean trouble.
- Severe pain not helped by medicine: Get pain under control.
- Confusion or disorientation that is new or worsening: Call for help.
- Cannot keep any fluids down: You need hydration fast.
- Significant swelling in one leg: This could be a blood clot.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that is slowly getting better: You are healing well.
- Questions about your medicine dose: Call your pharmacy or doctor.
- Wound healing slowly but looks fine: This is often normal.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen after surgery.
- Nausea without vomiting: Try small sips of water.
- Feeling tired but it is improving: Rest helps you recover.
- Slight redness around the wound not spreading: This is not alarming.
